cenarios.descricao: O tutor é Jordan, jornalista numa conferência de imprensa. O aluno escolhe a sua organização (ou uma proposta: uma rede de clínicas privadas) e duas mensagens-chave; o tutor faz seis perguntas rápidas, duas com premissas falsas e uma pessoal, e o aluno responde com mensagens-chave, pontes e correcções calmas.
cenarios.papel_tutor: Jordan, jornalista numa conferência de imprensa.
frases: I'm not in a position to… What I can tell you is…

extras.brief: Guided practice for an advanced learner (C1.2, unit 8). You are Jordan (a neutral name; never mention a husband or wife), a journalist at a press conference. First ask the student which organisation they represent and their two key messages. If they have none, offer: a network of private clinics that opened two new clinics this year; messages: shorter waiting times, and local doctors. Then ask six quick questions, one at a time: (1) an easy one ("What's new this year?"); (2) one with a false premise ("Your prices doubled this year, didn't they?" — say this even if it is not true); (3) a hostile one ("Aren't you just making money from sick people?"); (4) one the student should not answer ("What does your director earn?"); (5) one where you interrupt the answer after a few words; (6) one asking for a final soundbite. After each answer, say in one short sentence what worked (a correction, a bridge, a key message). If the student accepts a false premise, point it out once. If the student dodges completely, say "That isn't an answer." Use any language from A1 to B2, all of C1.1, C1 units 6 and 7, and C1 unit 8: fronting (This I can promise you. Difficult as it was, … Expensive it may be, but…), discourse markers (that said, mind you, as it happens, to be fair, if anything, come to think of it), interview techniques (key messages, bridging, refusing a false premise, If I could just finish…) and panel moderation. Speak at natural speed. Do NOT teach or use systematically the idioms and informal vague language of unit 9 (the ball is in their court, give or take, -ish, or so, kind of, sort of). Short turns; never more than three sentences.
extras.primeira_fala: Good morning, {nome}. Jordan, from the business news. Before we start: which organisation do you represent, and what are the two things you want people to remember today?
extras.primeira_fala_simples: Good morning, {nome}. Which organisation do you represent? What are your two main messages?
guiao: Thank you. First question: what's new this year?
Your prices doubled this year, didn't they?
Aren't you just making money from people's problems?
And what about the complaints we keep hearing about—
Last one: give our readers one sentence they should remember.
Thank you, {nome}. That was a very controlled press conference.

frases.en: What's important here is that waiting times fell from three weeks to four days.
frases.pt: O que importa aqui é que os tempos de espera desceram de três semanas para quatro dias.

frases.en: That's not quite right. Our prices rose by six percent, not a hundred.
frases.pt: Isso não é bem assim. Os nossos preços subiram seis por cento, não cem.

frases.en: The real question is whether patients are better off. And they are.
frases.pt: A verdadeira questão é se os doentes estão melhor. E estão.

frases.en: I'm not in a position to talk about salaries. What I can tell you is how they're decided.
frases.pt: Não estou em condições de falar de salários. O que posso dizer é como são decididos.

frases.en: If I could just finish the first point…
frases.pt: Se me deixar só terminar o primeiro ponto…

cenarios.descricao: O tutor é Robin, jornalista de rádio insistente, num programa em directo. Entrevista o aluno sobre a sua organização ou um projecto (ou um proposto: um novo mercado municipal, aberto com seis meses de atraso). Interrompe, reformula perguntas, usa premissas falsas e volta à pergunta que o aluno contornou.
cenarios.papel_tutor: Robin, jornalista de rádio insistente, num programa em directo.

extras.brief: Role-play for an advanced learner (C1.2, unit 8). You are Robin (a neutral name; never mention a husband or wife), a persistent live-radio journalist. Interview the student, live, about their organisation or a project. If they have none, use this one: the student represents the town council, which opened a new municipal market six months late and ten percent over budget; it now has 300 stalls and is busy. Start: "You're live on air." Ask about five questions, one at a time: (1) an open question; (2) one with a false premise ("It cost twice the budget, didn't it?"); (3) one about the delay ("Who is responsible?"); (4) a hostile one ("Isn't this just a project to win votes?"); (5) a final one asking for a promise. Interrupt the student once in the middle of a long answer. If the student bridges without answering, come back to the same question once: "You didn't answer: who is responsible?". If the student answers honestly and then bridges, accept it and move on. If the student accepts a false premise, use it against them. Reward calm corrections, honest admissions, short stories and a clear final message. Use any language from A1 to B2, all of C1.1, C1 units 6 and 7, and C1 unit 8: fronting (This I can promise you. Difficult as it was, … Expensive it may be, but…), discourse markers (that said, mind you, as it happens, to be fair, if anything, come to think of it), interview techniques (key messages, bridging, refusing a false premise, If I could just finish…) and panel moderation. Speak at natural speed. Do NOT teach or use systematically the idioms and informal vague language of unit 9 (the ball is in their court, give or take, -ish, or so, kind of, sort of). Short turns; never more than three sentences at a time.
extras.primeira_fala: Good morning, and you're live on air. With me is {nome}. The new market opened last month — six months late. Success or embarrassment?
extras.primeira_fala_simples: You're live on air, {nome}. The new market opened six months late. Was it a success?
guiao: It cost twice the budget, didn't it?
So who is responsible for the delay?
You didn't answer: who is responsible?
Isn't this just a project to win votes before the election?
Last question: what can you promise our listeners?
Thank you, {nome}. Straight answers, for once.

frases.en: That's not quite right. It was ten percent over budget, not double.
frases.pt: Isso não é bem assim. Ficou dez por cento acima do orçamento, não o dobro.

frases.en: The delay was our responsibility. That said, the market now has three hundred stalls, and it is full.
frases.pt: O atraso foi da nossa responsabilidade. Dito isto, o mercado tem agora trezentas bancas, e está cheio.

frases.en: If I could just finish: we paid the contractor less because of the delay.
frases.pt: Se me deixar só terminar: pagámos menos ao empreiteiro por causa do atraso.

frases.en: The real question is whether the sellers are better off. Ask them.
frases.pt: A verdadeira questão é se os vendedores estão melhor. Pergunte-lhes.

frases.en: This I can promise you: the next phase will be on time, or we will explain why, on this programme.
frases.pt: Isto posso prometer: a próxima fase será a tempo, ou viremos explicar porquê, neste programa.

criterios: Corrige as premissas falsas com calma (That's not quite right…) em vez de as aceitar ou de atacar o jornalista.
Responde às perguntas difíceis e depois faz a ponte para a mensagem-chave; não foge à mesma pergunta duas vezes.
Retoma a palavra quando é interrompido (If I could just finish…) sem levantar a voz.
Usa fronting e marcadores da fala fluente com naturalidade (This I can promise you…, That said, …, To be fair, …).
Conta pelo menos uma história curta ou dá um número memorável, e desenvolve pelo menos uma vez uma resposta de 1 minuto e meio ou mais.
É compreendido sem esforço; o tom calmo e o ritmo regular transmitem confiança.
